boundary_condition: Treat as a soft default; if true afternoon return departures are unavailable, limited, or unattractive, consider options close to afternoon.
canonical_value: Prefer afternoon return-flight departures, with nearby times acceptable when true afternoon options are limited.
condition: When booking or comparing round-trip flights and selecting the return-leg departure time.
default_action: Search for return-flight options departing in the afternoon and present those first when available.
exception_condition: Do not apply as a universal outbound-leg rule; one supporting dialogue separately used a morning outbound while still preferring an afternoon return.
name: afternoon_return_departure_preference
preference_value: Prefer the return flight to depart in the afternoon.
rationale: Multiple supporting utterances indicate a soft preference for afternoon timing on the return leg, sometimes alongside outbound timing. Keep as a return-departure timing default without generalizing it to all outbound flights.

boundary_condition: Applies only as a non-exclusive airline preference; United is favored only among otherwise suitable options and may coexist with other acceptable preferred carriers.
canonical_value: United is a soft preferred airline option, not an exclusive carrier requirement.
condition: When searching for commercial flights and no stronger current-trip carrier instruction overrides this preference.
default_action: Give United positive ranking weight and include United among preferred carrier options when otherwise comparable, while still considering other suitable airlines.
exception_condition: If United is unavailable, worse on primary itinerary constraints such as nonstop/timing/class, materially less attractive, or the user explicitly requests another carrier for the current trip, use or present the better alternative.
name: soft_united_preferred_carrier
preference_value: United is a soft preferred/acceptable airline, not an exclusive carrier requirement.
rationale: Kept as a soft, non-exclusive United carrier preference. It is supported by repeated examples naming United among acceptable or preferred airlines, while also explicitly allowing other carriers. It should not be merged with Delta because United and Delta are different carrier values and can both be acceptable preferences rather than true aliases or a required default/fallback pair.

boundary_condition: This is a soft preference: Delta is favored only among otherwise suitable options and may coexist with other acceptable preferred carriers.
canonical_value: Delta is a soft preferred airline option, not an exclusive carrier requirement.
condition: When choosing among flight carriers and Delta is available while also satisfying the trip's schedule, route, price, and stop constraints.
default_action: Search for or present Delta options as part of the preferred carrier set, and favor Delta when it is otherwise comparable to alternatives.
exception_condition: Use another acceptable carrier when Delta is unavailable, materially worse, or does not meet the current trip constraints.
name: soft_delta_preferred_carrier
preference_value: Delta is a preferred airline to include in the flight shortlist, but not an exclusive carrier requirement.
rationale: Kept as a soft, non-exclusive Delta carrier preference. The evidence repeatedly supports including or favoring Delta when feasible, but not treating Delta as the only acceptable airline. It should not be merged with United because they are distinct carrier values, not aliases, and the evidence permits multiple preferred carriers.

boundary_condition: Applies only to flight departure time-of-day. Do not infer it for arrival times, dates, routes, every leg automatically, or earliest-afternoon departures as a recurring rule.
canonical_value: Prefers afternoon flight departures as a soft default when no different departure-time constraint is specified.
condition: When selecting or comparing flight departure times.
default_action: Look first for departure options in the afternoon; follow any current explicit request for another time window or exact time.
exception_condition: If acceptable afternoon departures are unavailable or conflict with other stated constraints, ask before broadening to nearby time windows.
name: prefers_afternoon_departures
preference_value: Prefers flight departures in the afternoon when no different departure-time constraint is specified.
rationale: Multiple examples across separate conversations show the user asking for afternoon flight departures. Keep as a soft departure-time default, limited to flight departure time and overridden by any explicit current constraint.

boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
canonical_value: Prefer window seats on flights when a seat-location preference can be applied.
condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
rationale: Multiple source examples directly state a preference for a window seat on flights, making this a grounded longitudinal seat-location preference rather than a one-off constraint.

boundary_condition: Use this as a soft preference, not an absolute requirement, because the evidence ranges from a direct requirement to a tentative request and a later verification question.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
condition: When evaluating or booking a hotel, treat free breakfast as a recurring included-service preference.
default_action: Prioritize or verify hotels with free breakfast when available; if breakfast is not listed, ask or check rather than assuming it is included.
exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely for lacking free breakfast unless the user explicitly makes it required in the current booking; do not infer a full or high-quality breakfast requirement unless stated.
name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
rationale: Multiple examples show the user asking for or verifying free hotel breakfast. The evidence supports a recurring soft included-service preference, but not an absolute requirement or any specific breakfast quality/type.

boundary_condition: Treat this as a reusable hotel-amenity preference, not a destination, date, price, restaurant/bar, or indoor/outdoor pool preference. Use it as soft unless the current request makes the amenities mandatory.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise access.
condition: When selecting or evaluating hotel options.
default_action: Prioritize or verify hotels that offer all three amenities: a pool, a hot tub, and fitness or exercise access; clearly note if one is missing.
exception_condition: If otherwise suitable hotels do not offer all three amenities, present close matches while explicitly noting which of pool, hot tub, or fitness/exercise access is absent.
name: prefer_hotel_pool_hot_tub_fitness
preference_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise access.
rationale: The examples consistently ask for hotel pool, hot tub, and exercise/fitness access. This is a reusable hotel-amenity preference. The indoor/outdoor pool detail appears in only one example and should not be generalized here.

boundary_condition: Treat this as a durable amenity preference, not a destination-, date-, party-size-, or price-specific requirement. Do not infer indoor versus outdoor pool preference unless the user states it for the current trip.
canonical_value: Prioritize hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise facility.
condition: When choosing or evaluating a hotel for a stay.
default_action: Prioritize hotel options that include all three wellness/recreation amenities: a pool, a hot tub, and a fitness center or comparable place to exercise.
exception_condition: Relax the preference or ask for clarification if no suitable hotel offers all three amenities, or if the user explicitly deprioritizes recreation or exercise amenities for the current booking.
name: prefers_hotels_with_pool_hot_tub_and_fitness_options
preference_value: Hotels that offer a pool, a hot tub, and a fitness center or comparable exercise facility.
rationale: Multiple hotel-search examples independently state a preference for a pool, hot tub, and exercise/fitness facility. Indoor versus outdoor pool details are mixed and should not be promoted to a hard memory, but the shared wellness/recreation amenity bundle is durable enough to keep.

boundary_condition: Do not infer specific cuisine, star rating, bar service, kid-friendliness, downtown location, ski access, or wooded setting unless stated for the current trip.
canonical_value: Value hotel options with convenient on-site or nearby restaurant access.
condition: When searching for, comparing, or summarizing hotel options.
default_action: Mention on-site or nearby restaurant availability and use convenient dining access as a soft tie-breaker rather than a hard filter.
exception_condition: Do not apply if the user explicitly deprioritizes dining access or if stronger current-trip constraints override it.
name: hotel_restaurant_access
preference_value: Hotels with on-site or nearby restaurant access, with restaurant availability noted during comparisons.
rationale: Several hotel-related examples mention wanting on-site or nearby restaurant access or information. Because some evidence is contextual and varies in specificity, this should remain a soft dining-access preference rather than a hard filter or a claim about particular cuisine, rating, or setting.

boundary_condition: Do not generalize this into a broad amenity-rich or atmosphere preference. Do not infer destination, dates, price, balcony, ocean view, restaurant/bar, or indoor/outdoor pool type from this habit.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise access.
condition: When selecting or evaluating hotel options.
default_action: Prioritize or verify hotel properties with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise access before recommending or booking.
exception_condition: If a current trip prioritizes another tradeoff or a property lacks one of these amenities, ask whether a close substitute or omission is acceptable.
name: prefer_hotel_pool_hot_tub_fitness
preference_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise access.
rationale: Multiple examples support a recurring hotel amenity preference for pool, hot tub, and exercise access. Wording varies between must-have and preference, so keep it as a soft default that verifies or prioritizes these amenities without inferring unrelated amenities or trip details.

boundary_condition: Use this as a soft included-service preference. Do not infer breakfast quality, full breakfast, destination, dates, price, room setup, or other amenities from this habit.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
condition: When searching for, evaluating, or choosing a hotel.
default_action: Favor hotels that advertise free breakfast when otherwise suitable options are available; verify availability if breakfast inclusion is unclear.
exception_condition: If no otherwise suitable hotel includes free breakfast, or if the current request treats breakfast only tentatively, ask whether a hotel without free breakfast is acceptable rather than rejecting good options outright.
name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
rationale: The examples show repeated interest in hotels with free breakfast, though one mention is tentative and one is phrased as a question. Keep as a soft hotel-selection default rather than a hard requirement.

boundary_condition: This is a soft customer/review-rating default, not an exact 4-star-only rule, not a hotel-class-star requirement, and not a reusable 4.5-star or 3.5-star threshold by itself.
condition: When searching for hotels and a Google rating, review score, or similar customer-facing rating is available, especially for nice, upscale, resort-style, or high-rated stays.
default_action: Filter or rank toward hotels with customer-facing ratings of at least 4.0 stars and report the rating source when known.
exception_condition: If the user specifies a different threshold, prioritizes a budget stay with an explicit lower floor such as 3.5 stars, asks for the cheapest option regardless of quality, only suitable options fall below 4.0, or the rating metric is unclear, follow or clarify the current trip-specific instruction instead of hard-enforcing the 4.0 default.
name: hotel_four_star_customer_rating_floor
preference_value: Prefer hotels with clearly good customer-facing ratings, normally at least 4.0 stars, while treating higher ratings such as 4.5 as a bonus and lower stated floors as trip-specific exceptions.
rationale: Both candidates describe the same reusable hotel quality-threshold habit. The repeated, well-grounded signal is a soft 4.0+ customer-facing rating floor; the 4.5-star mention is only an ideal upgrade, and the 3.5-star mention is a trip-specific budget exception rather than a separate default.

boundary_condition: Evidence supports queen-size beds as the recurring preference. A king bed may be acceptable when explicitly offered or requested, but the evidence does not establish a reusable preference to upgrade to king whenever possible.
condition: When booking a standard hotel room where a single larger/shared bed is appropriate and no separate-bed setup has been requested.
default_action: Filter for or request a queen-size bed when bed type is selectable; if the listing only shows double, twin, or unspecified bedding, confirm the bed setup before booking.
exception_condition: Honor explicit requests for twin beds, multiple separate beds, multiple rooms with different bedding, accessibility-related bedding, or any other trip-specific bed arrangement.
name: queen_bed_for_single_bed_hotel_rooms
preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for hotel rooms intended to have one larger/shared bed.
rationale: Multiple hotel-room requests specify a queen-size bed or at least queen-size bedding when a single larger bed is appropriate. Preserve this as a soft reusable default, without generalizing to a standing king-bed upgrade or overriding explicit separate-bed arrangements.

boundary_condition: Do not treat balcony as mandatory unless the current request explicitly says it is required. Do not infer an ocean view or any specific view from the balcony preference alone.
canonical_value: Prefer a hotel room with a balcony, especially when the room is above the first floor or the floor is unknown; a first-floor room can waive the balcony preference.
condition: Use when searching for, booking, or evaluating hotel room amenities, particularly when the room is above the first floor or the floor has not been specified.
default_action: Ask for or verify that the hotel room has a balcony as a soft default preference.
exception_condition: If the room is on the first floor, the balcony preference may be waived.
name: hotel_room_balcony_preference
preference_value: Prefers a hotel room with a balcony when booking or evaluating rooms.
rationale: Supported by multiple hotel-room amenity requests mentioning a balcony, with one explicit flexibility condition that a first-floor room does not need one. The evidence supports a soft balcony preference rather than an always-mandatory requirement, and does not justify adding an ocean-view requirement.

boundary_condition: Do not infer that the user always wants nonstop first, wants a layover for price reasons, or wants to add a stop to break up a long route unless the current request says so.
canonical_value: When a flight itinerary includes or may need a connection, prefer at most one short layover.
condition: When evaluating flight itineraries where a connection is acceptable, necessary, or being considered.
default_action: Favor itineraries with at most one short layover; ask before selecting itineraries with multiple layovers or a long layover.
exception_condition: Override this default if the user explicitly requests nonstop only, requests a longer stopover, or prioritizes schedule, availability, price, or another constraint over layover count or layover duration.
name: flight_single_short_layover_preference
preference_value: Prefers connecting itineraries with no more than one layover, and for any layover to be short enough for a comfortable transfer rather than prolonged.
rationale: Supported as a soft connecting-flight policy: the evidence consistently favors limiting connections to no more than one and avoiding long layovers when a layover is acceptable or needed. It does not require merging contrasting alternatives, and the boundary preserves that this is not a universal nonstop-only or price-driven rule.

boundary_condition: Do not generalize this to other amenities such as microwave, balcony, bar, fireplace, room size, location, dates, or price.
canonical_value: Prefers hotel rooms with both an in-room coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
condition: When selecting or comparing hotel rooms and in-room amenities are being considered.
default_action: Use an in-room coffee maker and refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft amenity criteria, and confirm availability when relevant.
exception_condition: If a hotel otherwise strongly matches the current trip, treat a missing coffee maker or refrigerator/mini-fridge as a point to confirm with the user rather than an automatic rejection.
name: hotel_room_coffee_maker_and_fridge_preference
preference_value: Prefers a hotel room with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
rationale: Repeated evidence across hotel conversations supports a reusable soft preference for rooms with both a coffee maker and refrigerator/mini-fridge. It is not a hard requirement and should not be generalized to unrelated amenities.

boundary_condition: Treat this as a soft default unless the user explicitly makes breakfast mandatory. Do not infer a required breakfast quality standard from this preference alone.
canonical_value: Prefers hotels that include free breakfast.
condition: When searching for or comparing hotels for an overnight trip, after satisfying explicit core constraints such as location, room or bed needs, budget, and required hotel class.
default_action: Rank or surface hotels with free breakfast higher, and confirm whether a candidate includes it when the amenity is not clear.
exception_condition: Relax or ignore this preference if the user says breakfast is unimportant, if no suitable hotel meets higher-priority constraints with free breakfast, or if the user knowingly chooses a hotel without it.
name: prefer_hotels_with_included_breakfast
preference_value: Prefer a hotel that includes free breakfast.
rationale: Multiple hotel examples show interest in included breakfast. The evidence supports a reusable preference, but wording varies in strength, so it should remain a soft default rather than a mandatory filter or a claim about breakfast quality.
